description: A governing proxy in front of HubSpot's official MCP server — the Eclipse WRAP posture for the customer family. HubSpot's server (GA 2026-04-13) reads and writes 12 object types including Service Hub tickets, acting as the signed-in user with no approval gate; Orbit adds the layer that asks. A pinned classification registry tiers every vendor tool: unclassified vendor tools are invisible to clients, and vendor T3 tools (delete, bulk) are classified but never surfaced in v1. If a vendor tool's tier rises under the wrap, the proxy halts it and emits a notice receipt until an owner clears the halt by name. T2 tools (ticket reply send, deal stage move) require approval tokens bound to the tool plus the exact arguments hash; all results are masked at egress; every call lands in a hash-chained, content-free receipt ledger. HubSpot custom objects are a declared gap — absent from the vendor tool set and never reached around. C0 is proven against a local HubSpot-shaped stub vendor, including both drift fixtures.
